data.name: Jalam
data.gender_notes: Jalam is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: In Hindu mythology, Jalam is derived from the Sanskrit word ‘Jal’, which means ‘water’ or ‘rain’. This name is often associated with Lord Indra, the deity of rain and thunder. It is believed that the name Jalam carries the blessings of Lord Indra, who brings life-giving rain and prosperity. The name Jalam carries the meaning “Water, Rain” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Jalam usually hope their child will grow to embody water, rain and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: A symbol of renewal, purification, and abundance.
data.etymology: Jalam belongs to the Sanskrit linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Water, Rain.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Jalam total 1, giving a life-path number of 1. Number 1 is linked with Sun and with the qualities of leadership, independence and initiative.

data.cultural_impact: Jalam is a name that resonates with the lush, green landscapes and vibrant agricultural traditions of India. It represents the essence of life, as water is essential for the growth of crops and sustenance of all forms of life. In Hindu society, the name Jalam is often associated with festivals and rituals that celebrate the abundance of water and the blessings of Lord Indra. For instance, during the rainy season, many Indians celebrate the festival of Raksha Bandhan, where they make offerings to Lord Indra to ensure a prosperous monsoon.
data.spiritual_significance: From a spiritual perspective, the name Jalam carries the blessings of Lord Indra, the deity of rain and thunder. It is believed that the name invokes the divine energies of the Lord, who can bring happiness, prosperity, and protection to those who call upon him. In Hindu scriptures and folklore, Lord Indra is known to be a powerful and generous deity, who showers his devotees with His blessings and salvages them from calamities. The name Jalam, therefore, is a reminder of the divine connection between humans and nature, and the importance of revering and respecting the natural elements of the world.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Jalam signifies the purifying and nurturing element of water in Hinduism. It embodies the fluidity of change and the cyclical nature of life. The name Jalam is a reminder of the importance of water in maintaining balance and harmony within oneself and the universe.
